subject: Commercial timing: invoice phasing, min-commit, and tax responsibility
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Feb 2027 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Acuity — commercial timing / action items before legal review

Hi team,

Following the demo last week, Acuity (prospect) sent back an Order Form with commercial redlines. High level asks from procurement:
- They want monthly invoicing in arrears, but also asked to remove the 25% upfront.
- Request to move minimum commit to an annual number with quarterly true-ups.
- Net terms: they propose Net 60. Finance prefers Net 45 or Net 30 depending on region.
- Tax: they want Redwood to absorb any VAT/GST charges in EU and provide evidence.

Attached: Acuity_OrderForm_Redlines.docx (they returned tracked changes).

Can Legal (Karthik) and Sales Ops (Ben) weigh in on acceptability and a compromise we can present? Goal is to keep the deal live this month and avoid multi-week redline cycles.

Key asks from me: recommended stance on upfront deposit, net terms, and language around customer tax responsibility vs. Redwood providing tax evidence.

Thanks — Camila

--
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com
From: Sophie Alvarez <sophie.alvarez@acuityhealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: AcuityHealth Procurement <procurement@acuityhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Feb 2027 10:20:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Acuity Order Form — redlines attached

Camila,

Thanks for the walkthrough. Attached is our redlined Order Form. A few notes to call out explicitly so there is no confusion:
- We do not want an upfront deposit — Acuity budgets monthly and needs flexibility for the pilot.
- Minimum commit: we can do an annual minimum but would like a quarterly true-up so spend is aligned to usage.
- Invoicing cadence: monthly in arrears is non-negotiable for us.
- Net terms: Net 60 is standard for our vendors.
- Taxes: Acuity is VAT-registered in EU; we expect vendor to be responsible for collecting/proving VAT handling (we will provide VAT ID upon request).

Please confirm if Redwood can accept these items or propose alternatives. We are trying to finalize legal this week.

Attachments: Acuity_OrderForm_Redlines.docx (redline comments inline)

Best,
Sophie Alvarez
Senior Procurement Manager
AcuityHealth
sophie.alvarez@acuityhealth.com
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 14:40:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Acuity Order Form — redlines attached

Karthik — forwarding Acuity's redlines with a short summary of what procurement is asking and our commercial goals.

Summary for legal review:
- Remove 25% upfront? Customer wants monthly in arrears only.
- Move min-commit to annual, but they want quarterly true-ups.
- Net 60 requested; Finance would prefer Net 45.
- VAT/GST: they expect vendor handling + evidence. They said they will give VAT ID.

Ask: can Legal propose contract language that preserves our ability to require an initial deposit for onboarding while giving Acuity the monthly invoicing they need? Also need language that clarifies tax responsibility and evidence exchange (what is acceptable proof of VAT handling).

If you can draft a single-sheet summary of redline responses we can send back to Acuity, that would help speed this along.

Thanks — Camila

On Mon, Feb 1, 2027 at 10:20 AM Sophie Alvarez <sophie.alvarez@acuityhealth.com> wrote:
> (see attached redlines)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Feb 2027 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acuity Order Form — redlines attached

Camila — thanks for the context and the redlines. High-level legal position and recommended compromise below:

1) Upfront deposit: propose a reduced onboarding fee (25% of the first quarter) framed as a refundable credit against the first invoices. This preserves cashflow protection for Redwood while giving Acuity the monthly invoices they need.

2) Minimum commit / true-up: agree to annual minimum with explicit quarterly usage true-ups. Add a cap on retroactive true-up exposure (one quarter lookback) so neither party is exposed to unlimited adjustments.

3) Net terms: counter to Net 45 (Finance preference). Offer Net 45 as our standard for this deal but accept Net 60 only for signed enterprise accounts with procurement-approved credit terms. If they insist on Net 60, we require an increased onboarding deposit (35%) or a credit check / PO guarantee.

4) Taxes: standard clause — customer is responsible for taxes to the extent required by law; Redwood will invoice without VAT where customer provides valid VAT registration evidence. In EEA cases where Redwood is required to collect VAT, we will calculate VAT on invoices and provide tax receipts. Request: have them upload VAT certificate prior to first invoice.

I attached a tracked-change Order Form with these changes (redlines_legal_v2.docx). Suggested approach: send a short, negotiable one-page summary to Sophie that lists the four points above and asks which option they prefer on Net terms (Net 45 + 25% onboarding vs Net 60 + 35% onboarding / PO).

—Karthik

Attachments: redlines_legal_v2.docx
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Feb 2027 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Acuity Order Form — invoicing mechanics and PO notes

Quick finance sanity check:
- If we accept monthly in arrears with only a small onboarding credit, we need clear PO/approval path. Many of their contracts go through a 6–8 week PO processing window; if Net 60 + no deposit, we'll carry material DSO exposure.
- Ops prefers structure: 25% onboarding (refundable as credit), then monthly invoices in arrears. If they require Net 60, require PO on file before first month and increase onboarding to 35%.
- For tax handling, we can accept customer-provided VAT certificate and invoice without VAT where appropriate; Finance needs a checklist of evidence to accept VAT-exempt status.

I'll prepare a short billing playbook for Camila to attach to the one-page summary to Acuity — includes PO checklist and required tax docs.

—Ben
Billing Operations Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Sophie Alvarez <sophie.alvarez@acuityhealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: AcuityHealth Procurement <procurement@acuityhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Feb 2027 16:30:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Acuity Order Form — redlines attached

Camila / team,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and proposed compromises. Acuity agrees to the following:
- 25% onboarding fee refundable as credit against the first invoice (we can accept this).
- Annual minimum with quarterly true-ups and a one-quarter lookback cap — agreed.
- Net terms: we can accept Net 45 if you can confirm PO processing will not delay first billing (we will issue a confirmation PO immediately upon signature).
- VAT: we will upload our VAT registration certificate prior to signing; Acuity will accept vendor invoices without VAT if Redwood confirms tax handling on the invoice.

Please send the DocuSign link (or updated redline) and we will route to legal for final sign-off. Attached is our tax certificate.

Attachments: tax_cert_Acuity.pdf

Best,
Sophie Alvarez
Senior Procurement Manager
AcuityHealth
